speaker: Pat
text: For the record, our view is that the amendment needed a signature. I'd rather not spend the morning on that.

speaker: Sandy
text: Ours is that Fawn had authority. Noted on both sides. Let's move on.

speaker: Sam
text: Sandy, can you walk us through what the next month looks like for you if nothing changes?

speaker: Sandy
text: The oak supplier wants one point four million by the fifteenth. Miss it and they cut me off on every job. Then payroll fails.

speaker: Sam
text: So the supplier date matters more than the total. Is that fair?

speaker: Sandy
text: That's fair.

speaker: Morgan
text: And the house. Sandy has been told the bank will take it if the business goes under.

speaker: Jordan
text: Pat, same question. What does the next month look like on your side?

speaker: Pat
text: We have a lakefront property under contract and a hotel partnership that closes in three weeks. Both need cash I don't have if I pay the full amendment.

speaker: Riley
text: Why do both have to close now? Could one wait?

speaker: Pat
text: The lakefront seller has another buyer. The hotel could probably slip a month.

speaker: Riley
text: So the lakefront is the priority.

speaker: Pat
text: Yes.

speaker: Sam
text: Let me sum up. Sandy needs the supplier paid by the fifteenth and wants to keep the house. Pat needs the lakefront to close and would like the hotel too.

speaker: Sandy
text: And both of us would rather keep working together.

speaker: Jordan
text: Here are three packages. One: we pay one point four by the fifteenth and the rent stays as is. Two: we pay one point two now, two hundred in sixty days, and you take two months' rent off. Three: we pay one point four, you sign on for both spring projects at a ten percent discount.

speaker: Morgan
text: Which of those do you prefer?

speaker: Jordan
text: Three, honestly. It keeps our spring on schedule.

speaker: Sandy
text: Three works if the one point four lands by the fifteenth. The discount is fine; I want the work.

speaker: Pat
text: It can land by the fourteenth if the escrow releases Monday.

speaker: Riley
text: What about the loan? Two hundred at ten percent.

speaker: Sam
text: What would help there?

speaker: Riley
text: Rolling it into the spring projects. Deduct it from the first invoice.

speaker: Pat
text: Done.

speaker: Morgan
text: And the house stays Sandy's?

speaker: Sandy
text: If the supplier is paid and the loan rolls, I don't need to sell. Yes.

speaker: Sam
text: So to check: one point four by the fourteenth, both spring projects at ten percent off, the loan deducted from the first spring invoice, rent unchanged. Anything missing?

speaker: Sandy
text: Put the four hundred dispute to rest in the same document. No one reopens it.

speaker: Pat
text: Agreed. We'll have it drafted by tonight.

speaker: Riley
text: Thank you. This went better than I expected.
